q1_issues.issue: 'That' is typed 'profit' although nothing in the text says the compared figure is a profit — 'a year-earlier profit' types only the comparandum — so this asserts a kind world knowledge supplies; the antecedentless-pronoun rule would give 'thing' absent a text-supplied kind.

The appositive restatement 'or 13 cents a share' is stored as a second Measure on the SAME entity under the SAME scale 'profit', so one profit now carries two competing values (102000000 dollar, 13 cent_per_share) on one dimension, with nothing recording that they are one figure restated.
The measure scale 'profit' is the same word as the measured entity's own kind, so (Measure sk_profit_2 profit 102000000 dollar) reads as the profit's profit rather than its amount.

q2_gaps: appositional / reformulating 'or' ('$102 million, or 13 cents a share') — the Disjunction section treats every 'or' as inclusive-or-else-Xor and has no equative/restatement sense
a per-share (rate-denominated) restatement of a total — no way to mark two magnitudes as one value expressed on two denominators
a temporal modifier on an entity noun ('a year-earlier profit') — Time attaches to eventualities, so the anteriority can only be buried inside the fused compound symbol
a discourse-deictic 'That' pointing at a preceding sentence with no CONTEXT supplied — no antecedent exists to reuse and no licensed way to record the pointing
notes: 'compared with' correctly routes the NP into the prepositional-verb oblique (With) rather than a direct-object role, the stative intransitive subject takes Experiencer, and the compound decomposition emits the head genus without exposing the noun modifier. The parse's silent choice not to emit (Or ...) is the faithful reading but is not what the Disjunction section as written prescribes.
